questions.q: What does clicking the blue "+" button that appears when hovering over a diff line do?
options: Deletes that line permanently
Automatically approves the pull request
Starts an inline comment attached to that exact line, rather than a general comment on the whole PR
Reverts that line to its previous version
questions.explain: Inline comments anchor feedback to the precise line it concerns, which is their whole advantage over a general comment.

questions.q: What happens to a file's "Viewed" checkbox if the author pushes new commits that touch that file?
options: It unchecks automatically, signaling that something in that file changed since you last reviewed it
Nothing changes — Viewed stays checked regardless of new commits
The file is permanently removed from the diff
It automatically submits an Approve review
questions.explain: Viewed resetting on new commits is a deliberate signal to re-check a file whose content has since changed.

questions.q: What does submitting a review as "Request changes" do to a pull request?
options: Nothing — it's purely informational like a Comment
It automatically closes the pull request
It immediately reverts all commits in the PR
It explicitly blocks the merge until the requested changes are addressed
questions.explain: Request changes is the one verdict that formally blocks merging, unlike a plain Comment.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes a review comment like "this will throw if items is empty — worth a guard clause?" better than "this looks off"?
options: It's longer, and longer comments are always better
It uses more technical vocabulary
It's specific and actionable, pointing to the exact concern rather than a vague impression
There's no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Specific, actionable feedback tells the author exactly what to look at and why, rather than leaving them to guess.

questions.q: What does the "Approve" verdict in a review typically do, depending on a repository's branch protection rules?
options: It automatically deletes the branch
It has no practical effect at all, in any repository
It automatically requests a second review from someone else
It's often required before the merge button unlocks, signaling the reviewer is satisfied with the changes
questions.explain: Many repositories require at least one Approve before a PR can be merged, enforced via branch protection settings.
